refuted.claim: Design recommendation: 'Get 10^F for 0<=F<1 by Table Lookup (op T) into a 100- or 1000-entry table plus one linear interpolation' — and the algorithm table costs it as '1 lookup' alongside multiplies, i.e. as if it were cheap.
refuted.why: Op T is a LINEAR right-to-left scan, and its cost grows with table size. The manual says so outright ('Because the timing of the table lookup operation is determined by the number of characters in the table that are read before a table argument is found, it is desirable to have the least possible number of characters in the function') and the timing symbols make it quantitative: N = number of fields actually compared, and B on a table search 'includes only those argument fields actually compared and the intervening function values'. For the recommended 1000-entry table with a 3-digit argument and a 5-digit inline function, an average hit at entry 500 gives N=500, B = 500*3 + 499*5 = 3995, so T = 4.5(12 + 1 + 3995 + 1500) = 24.8 ms average, 49.5 ms worst case. That is TEN TIMES the cost of an 8x8 multiply (2.4 ms), and it would dominate the entire integration step. The 100-entry version is ~2.5 ms average — still no cheaper than a multiply.
refuted.correction: Do not search a uniform-grid transcendental table with op T. The grid is uniform and the argument digits ARE the index, so compute the entry address arithmetically and fetch with an indexed MLC: the 1410 has fifteen index registers (core 00025-00099, five positions each) and indexed addressing costs T = 34.5 us per single address indexed (30.67 us with the Accelerator), so an indexed 5-character MLC is roughly 4.5(12+1+5+5) + 34.5 = 138 us — about 180x cheaper than the 1000-entry T search and ~17x cheaper than a multiply. Reserve op T for genuinely non-uniform / unordered tables, where its right-to-left ordered scan is what you actually want.
refuted.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 'Table Lookup' pp.29-30 (timing T = 4.5(L+1+B+NA)), Figure 7 'Timing Formula Symbols' p.9 (definitions of N and of B on a table search), 'Indexing' p.14 (fifteen index registers, T = 34.5 per indexed address), '1410 Accelerator' p.96

refuted.claim: 'the same six mnemonics appear in the operation-code list of C28-0326-1 1410 Operating System Autocoder'

upgraded.claim: Table Lookup (op T) semantics as stated: A-address = rightmost position of search argument; B-address = rightmost character of the ENTIRE table; searched right to left; table argument must equal the search argument in length, a shorter one ends the table and turns on high-compare; stops one position LEFT of the first satisfying table argument so the B-address register ends holding the rightmost character of the function; L = 1, 6 or 12 with L=6 chaining the B-address and reusing the previous d-modifier; T = 4.5(L + 1 + B + NA). Word marks required on the leftmost position of the search argument and of every table field.

additions.claim: The 1410 Accelerator is an optional feature that changes EVERY timing formula in the manual: it cuts the memory cycle from 4.5 to 4.0 us and shortens data-operation cycle lengths, for ~23% internal speedup and 15-23% throughput gain. The accelerated arithmetic formulas are different in shape, not just scaled: Multiply T = 4[L + 1 + E + 2M + (2.5M + 1)(2A + 2)] and Divide T = 4[L + 1 + E + 6.5Q(2A + 2)]. For the 8-digit case that is ~1.62 ms per multiply and ~3.79 ms per divide, versus 2.37 / 5.44 ms unaccelerated. Any performance claim in the demo write-up must state which machine it assumes.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 '1410 Accelerator' pp.96-97; arithmetic recomputed in python3

additions.claim: Add/Zero-and-Add are roughly an order of magnitude cheaper than Multiply, which decides the algorithm shape. Add (two fields) T = 4.5(L + 1 + E + A + 1.5B + 1.5RB); Zero and Add (two fields) T = 4.5(L + 1 + E + A + 1.5B); E = 1 when L = 1, E = 0 when L = 11. For A = B = 8, L = 11, no recomplement: 4.5 * 32 = 144 us, against 2369 us for an 8x8 multiply — a 16:1 ratio. So a table fetch plus ONE interpolation multiply is the right shape, and any polynomial/series evaluation costing several multiplies per call is not.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 'Add (Two Fields)' p.17, 'Zero and Add (Two Fields)' p.18; arithmetic recomputed

additions.claim: The Table Lookup d-characters are a three-bit mask, not an arbitrary code: bit 1 = low, bit 2 = equal, bit 4 = high, ORed together. That is why d=3 is low-or-equal, d=5 is low-or-high, d=6 is equal-or-high, d=7 stops on any, and blank (0) never matches so the search runs to the end of the table. The SimH 7010 CPU implements exactly this ('if (cind & op_mod) break;' with cind set to 1/2/4 by the comparison), rejects any d with bits above 7 as an invalid opcode, and sets the high indicator (cind = 4) on hitting the end-of-table word mark. Knowing it is a mask makes the bracketing logic for interpolation deducible rather than guesswork.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf Figure 25 p.30, cross-checked against SimH i7010_cpu.c case OP_T (https://github.com/simh/simh, sims 7000-series i7010_cpu.c)

additions.claim: Indexing is the mechanism the design should be built on, and its cost is documented: fifteen index registers occupy core positions 00025-00099, five positions each (register 1 = 00025-00029 ... register 15 = 00095-00099); the index factor is an actual number, not an address, added to the tagged address if its sign is plus and subtracted if minus; overflow during indexing does not set the arithmetic overflow latch; word marks in the index-register area are ignored by indexing; positions 00025-00099 may be used as general storage if not needed for indexing. Timing T = 34.5 us for each single address indexed (30.67 us accelerated). Addresses that CANNOT be indexed: the X-control field of an M, L or U instruction, and the G (Store Address Register) instruction. On a 10K system the high-order position of any indexed address must contain a zero.

The Move family's word-mark termination is finer than 'through first word mark', and the distinction matters for the rescale idiom. MLC/MLN/MLZ/MLW (d = C/A/B/D) stop at the first word mark in EITHER the A- or the B-field. Separate variants stop on one field only: MLCA/MLNA/MLZA/MLWA (d = T/'/'/S/U) on the first A-field word mark, MLCB/MLNB/MLZB/MLWB (d = L/J/K/M) on the first B-field word mark. Single-position forms are MLNS=1, MLZS=2, MLCS=3, MLWS=4. MLZS's full manual name is 'Move Left Zones, Single Position' — it moves zone bits only, one position, which is what makes it a sign stamp. Move data timing T = 4.5(L + 1 + A + B), L = 1, 6 or 12.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 Figure 22 'Data Move d-Characters and Mnemonics' p.26, instruction summary appendix p.101ff, accelerated timing list p.97

additions.claim: The Autocoder spelling of the sign test is BZN with a d-operand, not a distinct mnemonic. Minus test: V(I)(B)K = BZN(I)(B)B or BZN(I)(B)-, 'branch if B-address has a B bit but no A bit'. Machine-developed-plus test: V(I)(B)B = BZN(I)(B)AB or BZN(I)(B)+, 'both B and A bits'. Also available: V(I)(B)S = BZN(I)(B)A (A bit but no B bit), and V(I)(B)2 = BZN(I)(B) (no B nor A bits, i.e. the unsigned-plus case). Since a machine-developed plus is always BA, the minus test alone is sufficient after arithmetic, but data read from cards can carry any of the three plus encodings.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 branch-on-condition d-character table pp.38-39, and Figure 11 p.16

additions.claim: The 7080 square-root Program Library entry is a stronger precedent than the finder credits, because it is explicitly a FIXED-POINT routine: 'THE MACRO CALLS UPON A CLASS B SUBROUTINE WHICH USES NEWTONS ITERATION METHOD TO DETERMINE THE SQUARE ROOT OF A NUMBER FROM ONE TO FIFTEEN SIGNIFICANT DIGITS. FORTRAN FLOATING POINT CODING AND SUBROUTINES ARE NOT REQUIRED. ROOT PRECISION IS CONTROLLED BY DECIMAL DEFINITION OF THE AUTOCODER RCD.' Size: 400 storage positions for the subroutine plus 35 positions in line per macro entry; source language 7080 Autocoder; author F. U. Voss, IBM DPD HQ, available 4th quarter 1963. That is direct evidence that IBM's house method for a transcendental on a variable-length decimal machine of this family was fixed-point Newton with programmer-chosen decimal precision — exactly the design the finder recommends — not a call into the FORTRAN float package.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/C20-1602-8_1410_pgmCatJun68.pdf — C20-1602-8, entry 7080-08.3.001 'SQUARE ROOT MACRO AND SUBROUTINE'

additions.claim: The 1410 FORTRAN compiler itself is Program Library item 1410-FO-945, and the catalogue states that its users MUST order 1410-FO-138, which 'includes the relocation loader and subroutines necessary for executing FORTRAN object programs'. Appendix C of the 1410-FO-138 material contains instructions for constructing and maintaining a FORTRAN library tape, and the descriptive information lives in the 1410-PR-108 addendum ('Addendum for FORTRAN and FORTRAN Subroutines') and 1410-PR-134. These are the exact document/tape identifiers to chase at CHM or elsewhere.

Contrary to the finder's flat 'no listing survives and none surfaced', the surviving PR-108 processor tape image DOES contain the FORTRAN system's built-in-function linkage table, with entry-point addresses: the character strings 'SIN 0~COS 0~LOG 0~EXP 0~SQRT 0~ATAN 0~ABS 2~XABS 2~INT 1~XINT 1~MOD 1~XMOD 1~MAX0 1~MAX1 1~XMAX0 1~XMAX1 1~MIN0 1~MIN1 1~XMIN0 1~XMIN1 1~FLOAT 2~XFIX 2~SIGN 1~XSIGN 1~DIM 1~XDIM 1' and a parallel table pairing those names with five-digit core addresses (FLOAT 13097, XFIX 13186, ABS 13165, XABS 13149, and SIN/COS/LOG/EXP/SQRT/ATAN all at 13123, i.e. a common dispatch entry). That is the compiler's name/address table rather than the routine bodies, so it does not by itself settle the algorithms — but it means the object-time package is worth disassembling from the tape image before declaring the 1410 EXP/ALOG/SQRT methods unrecoverable. Note also that this release names the log function LOG, not the ALOG of the later OS FORTRAN (C28-0328-3) — a within-1410 release difference, not a 1401 confusion.
additions.source: sky-visions PR-108 tape image (jpr108, http://www.sky-visions.com/ibm/ibm7010_soft.shtml), decoded character dump in the session scratchpad; strings located by grep. Compiler-vs-library distinction is my inference from the table's structure, not a documented statement.

additions.claim: Table Lookup leaves the A-address register at A-LW (the leftmost, word-marked position of the search argument), and during the search the C-address register holds the A-address so it can be reloaded for each table field. The finder's table records only the B-address register result. For a chained interpolation sequence (L=6 form reusing the previous d-modifier), knowing that the A-address register is left at A-LW rather than restored to the units position matters.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 'Table Lookup' instruction, 'Address Registers after Operation' p.30

additions.claim: Op-code spot-checks against the manual's own instruction descriptions, beyond the Table Lookup table (all confirmed): Add two-field mnemonic A, op code A, T = 4.5(L+1+E+A+1.5B+1.5RB), registers A-LW / B-LB. Subtract mnemonic S, op code S. Zero and Add mnemonic ZA, op code '?', one- and two-field forms. Zero and Subtract mnemonic ZS, op code '!'. Multiply mnemonic M, op code '@', L = 1/6/11, registers A-LA / B-LB. Divide mnemonic D, op code '%', L = 1/6/11, B-address register left at the tens position of the quotient. Move/Scan family op code D with the Figure 22 d-characters. Move Characters and Suppress Zeros mnemonic MCS, p.27, T = 4(L+1+4A) accelerated. Branch-on-condition op code V with d-characters 1 (word mark), 2 (no zones), B (zone AB), K (zone B), S (zone A), 3 (WM or no zones). Compare mnemonic C, T = 4.5(L+1+A+B), L = 1/6/11. Store Address Register op code G, cannot be indexed, T = 4(L+8.5) = 62 us accelerated. Note the collision worth flagging in any opcode table: Autocoder mnemonic D means Divide, while the machine op-code character D means Move/Scan.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf — A22-0526-3 pp.17-22, 25-30, 36-39 and the instruction summary appendix pp.101ff

additions.claim: One check the finder's validation section is missing: eq.(13) is the closed-form solution only for the NON-rotating, flat-earth, constant-gamma, drag-only problem Allen and Eggers set up, and only with their exponential atmosphere. If the demo integrates gravity or a varying flight-path angle, eq.(13) will diverge from the numeric answer by a real physical amount, not by integration error. Use it as a per-step check only for the drag-only configuration, and turn gravity off in the regression run.
additions.source: http://hpp.education/Lessons/MecaSpace/Files/AllenEggers.pdf — NACA Report 1381, derivation preceding eq.(13) (the equation is obtained by integrating dV/V = (C_D rho0 A / 2m sin theta_E) e^(-beta y) dy, with the assumptions stated on pp.5-6)

notes:
Method: verification was done against pdftotext text layers of the exact bitsavers PDFs (A22-0526-3, C28-0328-3, J24-1468-1, C28-0309-1, C28-0326-1, C20-1602-8, A22-6726) already cached in this session's scratchpad, plus the pi.job source, the NACA 1381 text, and the SimH 7010 CPU source. Every fact block in the findings was checked; the eleven 'verified' ones are all genuine primary-source reads except for the two page-number/figure-citation slips and the storage-capacity omission reported above.

1401-vs-1410 confusion hunt: I found none of substance. The specific traps I checked and cleared - Table Lookup (op T) is a genuine 1410 instruction with no 1401 equivalent, so citing it is correct; Multiply and Divide are described in A22-0526-3 as part of the machine, not as the optional Multiply-Divide feature the 1401 needs; the 4.5 us cycle and the 10K-80K capacities are 1410 figures, not 1401 ones; the B-bit-minus / BA-plus sign convention is stated in the 1410 manual itself rather than carried over. The one near-miss is the Move d-character citation, where the finder pointed at 'Move Characters and Suppress Zeros' - an instruction that exists on BOTH machines - instead of Figure 22; that is a wrong-figure error, not a wrong-machine error. The FORTRAN facts are correctly attributed to the 1410/7010 manuals throughout, and the 7080 square-root precedent is correctly flagged as a 7080 item.

What I could not reach or resolve: (1) the sign placement inside the C28-0328-3 f+2 real format remains unreadable - the text layer renders the two worked examples as '5l4159005i' and '3141590651', which is consistent with overpunches but does not resolve which positions carry them; C28-0328-1 (the earlier printing, also on bitsavers) has NO text layer at all - pdftotext returns an empty file - so it cannot settle it without OCR or page images. The finder's open question stands unchanged. (2) I did not disassemble the PR-108 tape image, so whether the EXP/LOG/SQRT bodies are actually present in it is unestablished; I only confirmed the name/address table is there. (3) I did not attempt a CHM catalogue query for 1410-FO-138.

Bottom line for the implementer: the documentary spine of the findings is sound and largely verified. The two changes that would actually alter the program are the Table Lookup cost refutation - a 1000-entry op-T antilog table would cost ~25 ms per call and wreck the step loop, so index the table arithmetically instead - and the corrected atmosphere constants (0.15546801 / 0.07773400).
